chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī narrated that from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A person in janabah and a deceased person come together in a place where there is only enough water for one of them. Which of the two has more right that the water be assigned to him? He said: The junub performs tayammum, and the deceased is washed with water.
And the way of reconciling between them is that it be understood as a matter of choice, because both are obligatory. So whichever of them is washed with the water available, that is permissible.

key_terms.التَّخْيِيرِ: legal option or choice between two valid alternatives
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the limited water available for purification
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person requiring ritual washing
key_terms.وَاجِبَانِ: two matters that are both obligatory
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: performs tayammum as a substitute for water-based purification

ai.seo_question: If there is only enough water for either a junub or a deceased person, who should receive the water in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling when limited water is available for only one of two obligations: ghusl for a junub or washing a deceased person. It states that the junub may perform tayammum while the deceased is washed, and also presents the juristic reconciliation that either may be chosen since both are obligatory.
